label: paragraph_title
text: STRIKE THREATS.

label: text
text: SEVERE PUNISHMENT.

label: text
text: A circular notice has been issued to all shipping companies by the Canton Strike Committee, reading, inter alia:—

label: text
text: notification issued by the Tour Chambers of Commerce in Canton and this Committee were made out for the purpose of safeguarding the patriotic movement of our people to enable them to achieve victory at an early date.

label: text
text: "...plan for breaking our movement the enemy have taken the navigation line as their first step, and that when they have succeeded in this step they will then carry out other extraordinary plans for breaking our strike, so we must show our strong opposition to the first step they have now taken, to cause them to fall in their attempt, thus frustrating their wicRed plane in some way or the other"

label: paragraph_title
text: “No Indulgence.”

label: text
text: "Besides having separately notified our subordinates to take every precaution, we are specially writing to inform you that you should refuse to do anything in connection with declarement at the Customs, or loading of cargo on behalf of any steamer which may be contrary to the Trade Rules, and that intentional offence will entail arrest of the offender for severe punishment, and the confiscation of his property. There will be no indulgence on our part in dealing with such a case, in order to safeguard the Rules, and to penetrate the real aim of our patriotic movement. You must therefore respect yourselves, and must not make yourselves too late for repentance."

label: text
text: (Signed) Canton-Hong Kong Strike Committee:

label: text
text: The Finnish Mercantile Marine includes at the present time a relatively large number of sailing vessels, namely, 541 vessels of more than 20 tons each, representing a total of 83,392 tons, and it is now reported from Helsingfors that the leading owners of such vessels have formed a society for the protection of their mutual interests under the name of the Finnish Sailing Ship Owners' Association.

label: text
text: One of the first aims of the association will be to watch very carefully any proposed legislation in regard to the conditions and hours of labour at sea, this being one of the burning questions of the moment. The association is seeking to get the owners of sailing ships in all the Baltic countries to unite in forming a general association for the purpose of fixing and maintaining freight rates in that region at a remunerative minimum. At the present time the fleets of the owners affiliated to the association represent a total of between 50,000 and 60,000 tons of Finnish sailing ships.

label: paragraph_title
text: FINNISH SAILING SHIP SOCIETY

label: paragraph_title
text:
DANISH IDLE TONNAGE
 $ ^{1} $ REDUCED.

label: text
text: A large reduction is reported from Copenhagen to have taken place in the idle tonnage laid up at Danish ports. On July 12, there were 34 steamers of a total of $7,000 tons laid up; on July 19, the figures were reduced to 10 and $5,000 tons respectively, and further to 12 and 21,000 tons on July 31.

label: text
text: The cause of the improvement in the Danish shipping position is attributed to the effects of the coast stoppage in England; since the outbreak of which about 900,000 tons of shipping is lying in English ports, which tomnage has to be replaced in another manner. At the same time the transport of coal from America has acted favourably in freight rates from transmarine port to Europe for corn and other goods. The freight routes of the Danish United Company, which had to be restricted to North and South America in the spring, are expected to be fully restored in the present month.

label: text
text: Cargo and passengers on the Hong Kong-Canton Steamboats yesterday were very encouraging, both on the "up" and "down" boat. It is felt that an improvement has set in since the withdrawal of the strike pickets from the river.

label: text
text: The reason for the "holding up" of foreign shipping (mostly Japanese and Norwegian) on the Canton River a few days ago is the institution by the Bocca Tigris Forts of a system of examination which has not yet been put into actual operation. Steamers (other than the Hong Kong steamboats) are made to stop there for examination, if necessary. This is a Canton Government and not a strike measure.

label: text
text: The small gunboat "Fook Hoi," after going out past Bocca Tigris on a minelaying expedition (to guard against possible attack by Northern warships), is reported to have been captured by pirates. Other pirates are active up the East River.

label: text
text: A search is now being made near Yungki for the many bodies of those drowned when the Cantou-Kungyick tow-boat foundered (as reported by the "China Mail" correspondent at Pakkai).
